newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices ended lower on Friday amidst nervousness that Friday's dollar decline would erode demand for U.S. Treasuries and pressure European bonds.
Prices also fell in sympathy with German Bunds, undermined by continued speculation that the Bundesbank will raise rates.
One Swiss-based trader said his operations saw some new selling by a large institutional client. He added that the selling may pick up as investors return from holiday.
Elsewhere traders said Swiss bonds remained relatively expensive to swaps, citing a general degree of illiquidity which they said has plagued the market for months.
However, EuroSwiss futures on LIFFE were steady to firmer.

Swiss money market rates remained generally low in the very short maturities. The Swiss National Bank was seen keeping the market liquid, in an effort to counter any upward pressure on the Swiss franc.
Euro Swiss francs up one at 9842x.
